newsitem.title: UK: Regulators tighten noose around Railtrack.
newsitem.headline: Regulators tighten noose around Railtrack.

text.p: Britain's rail regulators said on Tuesday it had proposed modification of the license of rail infrastructure company Railtrack Plc to make it more accountable to the regulators.

The modifications will give regulators more enforcement powers if Railtrack, which manages Britain's sprawling network of railway tracks and stations, failed to deliver the revamped programme to which it had committed itself.

Railtrack's modified licence establishes a new General Duty on Railtrack in respect of maintenance, renewal and development of rail network and a series of further detailed and enforceable obligations in support of this duty.
The changes also give the regulators powers of investigation and enforcement if Railtrack fails to deliver without good reason.
The modified licence also makes it obligatory for Railtrack to consult with train operators and funders and meet their expectations.
Railtrack, which was listed on the London Stock Exchange last year in a 1.93 billion pounds($3.1 billion) equity sell-off, has been criticised for not investing enough in rail infrastructure.
Early this year the company unveiled a 15.9 billion pound package to maintain, renovate and take up new projects for Britain's railway system over the next 10 years.
Railtrack's share price, which has risen more than 80 percent since its flotation, closed at 779-1/2 pence on Monday. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
